stem: Which neck lump is most consistent with a midline, non-tender, soft, fluctuant, yellowish mass that is tethered to the overlying skin and does not move with tongue protrusion or swallowing?
explanation: Midline dermoid cyst is the best match. A midline, non-tender, soft or fluctuant, yellowish lesion that is tethered to the skin and does not move with swallowing or tongue protrusion is characteristic of a dermoid cyst.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Neck lumps

optionExplanations.A: Correct because a midline dermoid cyst is classically a soft, fluctuant, non-tender congenital lump that may be yellowish and tethered to the overlying skin, without movement on swallowing or tongue protrusion.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because reactive lymphadenopathy is usually mobile and tender and is commonly associated with recent infection.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a plunging ranula typically presents as a bluish cystic swelling arising from the floor of the mouth rather than a tethered midline neck lump.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a lymph node abscess would usually be painful, inflamed and tender rather than soft, calm and congenital in appearance.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a goitre moves with swallowing and is a thyroid swelling rather than a tethered midline dermoid cyst.
